name: Hawaii Commercial Foods Inc
old_description: Located in Maui, Hawaii, Hawaii Commercial Food Inc. offers Authentic Korean food from Busan.
about:
Hawaii Commercial Foods Inc. was founded in 2016 in Kahului, on the island of Maui, Hawaii. The company was established to bring authentic Korean flavors from Busan to the Hawaiian market, building on a family kimchi recipe handed down through generations.

The company handcrafts a line of traditional Korean side dishes, including kimchi, pickled vegetables such as jangachi, takuwan, and spicy pickled onion, as well as seaweed-based salads like wakame and namasu. Production takes place in a Maui facility where each item is prepared in small batches using the original recipe.

Hawaii Commercial Foods serves both retail and food-service customers, supplying grocery stores, restaurants, and direct consumers through an online store. Its products are positioned as authentic Korean pantry staples for the Hawaiian market and beyond.

The business emphasizes its generational recipe and handcrafted approach as its primary differentiators, distinguishing its offerings from mass-produced alternatives.

name: Hawaii Energy Connection
old_description: A leader in the Hawaii renewable energy market since 2007, Hawaii Energy Connection, LLC is
about:
Hawaii Energy Connection, LLC was founded in 2007 in Aiea, Hawaii. The company began as a solar photovoltaic integrator focused on the Hawaiian market.

The firm designs and installs turnkey solar PV systems for residential and commercial customers, pairing them with battery storage and energy management controls under its KumuKit™ brand. Services include system engineering, permitting, installation, and integration with utility grid-service programs such as the Smart Distributed Energy Resources (DER) tariff. The company handles projects from single-home rooftops to larger commercial arrays, though specific facility size and headcount are not disclosed.

Its customer base spans Hawaii homeowners seeking to reduce electricity bills and businesses requiring on-schedule, on-budget commercial solar deployments. The company also participates in emerging utility programs that allow aggregated edge-of-grid virtual power plants.

Hawaii Energy Connection distinguishes itself by right-sizing each system to maximize available incentives and peak production, and by managing the administrative paperwork that accompanies solar interconnection. It has been recognized on Inc. Magazine’s list of the 500 fastest-growing private companies in the U.S., ranking 16th in the energy sector.

about:
Hawaii Pacific X-Ray Corporation was founded in 1986 in Honolulu, Hawaii, as a partnership between Bill Johnson, a 30-year veteran of General Electric Medical Systems sales in the islands, and his son Chris Johnson. The pair set out to create a locally owned alternative to the entrenched x-ray sales and service providers then dominating the Hawaii and Pacific Basin markets.

The company operates as a distributor and service provider for diagnostic imaging equipment, offering sales, repairs, and supplies to medical facilities across Hawaii and parts of the Pacific Basin. Its product portfolio spans equipment from partners such as Hologic, Shimadzu Medical Systems, Ziehm Imaging, UMG/Del Medical, Konica Minolta Healthcare, and Mavig, covering breast and skeletal imaging as well as women's health systems.

Customers include hospitals, clinics, and imaging centers throughout the Hawaiian Islands and the wider Pacific region. The firm's supplier relationships give it direct access to major manufacturers, allowing it to support a range of clinical specialties from general radiology to mammography and interventional imaging.

The founders framed the business around a simple premise: that the success of their customers drives their own. They emphasize honest, prompt, and reliable service, long-term partnerships with both suppliers and clients, and a willingness to adopt new technologies and training to stay current in a rapidly evolving field.

name: Hawaii Technology Development Corporation (HTDC)
old_description: HTDC is a dynamic state agency driving Hawaiʻi’s economic diversification by fostering innovation, developing talent, and providing capital.
about:
Hawaii Technology Development Corporation (HTDC) is a state economic development agency headquartered in Honolulu, Hawaii. Created legislatively in 1983, it operates as an attached agency to the Department of Business, Economic Development & Tourism (DBEDT). The corporation was established to develop Hawaii's technology sector and diversify the state's economy.

HTDC does not manufacture products. Instead, it provides a range of services to foster innovation and support businesses across the islands. As Hawaii's Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MEP) center, its INNOVATE Hawaii program enhances productivity and technical performance of small and medium-sized manufacturers. The agency also operates the Hawaii Center for Advanced Transportation Technologies (HCATT), which has over 20 years of hydrogen and fuel cell research in partnership with the U.S. Air Force. HTDC offers co-working space, educational programs, funding opportunities, mentoring, and workforce development initiatives. It reports assisting over 300 companies and helping create more than 3,000 jobs, with $62 million in federal funding secured and $72 million in funding obtained.

HTDC serves technology startups, manufacturers, and energy companies across Hawaii. Its manufacturing assistance reaches small and medium-sized manufacturers statewide. The energy tech program focuses on hydrogen and fuel cell research for national and state needs. The agency also supports aerospace and ocean technology entrepreneurs, as highlighted in recent news about efforts to stem outmigration of young talent. Customers include startups seeking incubation, manufacturers needing technical guidance, and research organizations pursuing clean energy integration.

HTDC was created to address the need for a dedicated state entity to build a sustainable technology and innovation ecosystem. Its differentiating role is as a public-sector catalyst that connects businesses with capital, infrastructure, mentoring, and federal partnerships to accelerate commercialization and job creation in high-value sectors.

name: Heights Woodworking
old_description: Heights Woodworking has been making custom doors, windows and cabinets since 1946.
about:
Heights Woodworking operates from a 14,000-square-foot shop beside the Gowanus Canal in the Park Slope neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York. The business traces its roots to 1946, when Amor Villar founded the Heights Carpenter and Paint Shop to serve the borough’s brownstone owners with handcrafted doors, windows, cabinets, and stairs. In recent years, contractor and designer Jonas Sigle assumed leadership, bringing three decades of New York construction experience to the operation.

The company produces custom architectural millwork entirely by hand, from historic weight-and-chain windows and curved sash to staircases, cabinetry, and moldings matched to original Brooklyn profiles. Its 18,000-square-foot warehouse houses modern machinery alongside traditional joinery stations, staffed by more than 20 craftsmen with a combined 60-plus years of shop experience. Typical projects — ranging from trimming Ikea shelves to fabricating high-end Manhattan storefronts — are completed in two to three weeks.

Heights Woodworking serves homeowners, architects, designers, and contractors across the five boroughs, as well as commercial and institutional clients. The firm is an approved contractor for the New York Landmarks Conservancy, a designation that underscores its work on historic preservation projects. References and free estimates are standard practice.

Villar’s original vision — to provide the finest fabrication for the neighborhood — remains the guiding principle. The shop sources certified sustainable lumber, uses low-VOC adhesives and finishes, and maintains an in-house architect to translate concepts into buildable plans. An unconditional guarantee on quality and workmanship backs every piece.
